contract: Migration 019 stores operational one-use replica grants separately from primary map_sessions. A primary cascade removes all replicas. Grants bind both server tokens, primary connection, target endpoint, map/X/Z and all three pinned catalogs.

Only the exact loaded/ready primary can authorize the complete source-derived neighboring-server set. Every target must have an active published IPv4/port and owner token. Unconsumed grants expire after 60 seconds; repeating the same request does not extend expiry. A new route decision may renew retired or expired unconsumed grants.

Secondary CONNECT consumes an exact grant once under the account lock. Wrong endpoint, channel, primary generation, target token, absent/expired/replayed grant is rejected. Concurrent consumption has one winner and returns an explicit replica role.

A replica validates the complete supported no-recall ENTERCHAR summary and grant location, then acknowledges World. It holds only that summary; it cannot load the durable primary graph, claim primary cell ownership, save/checkpoint primary state or release current-user ownership.

World sends final CONRESULT only to the primary. A hydrated replica accepts original client CONREADY without an invented verdict or client CHARINFO/CONNECT. Only primary snapshots become AOI actors and movement broadcasters; replica movement updates local state only. Other secondary gameplay remains unported and cannot use a fabricated complete graph.

A native primary emits CHGCHANNEL then complete CHARINFO upon World CHARINFO while loaded, before CONNECT. Repeated initial metadata is ignored and CONREADY does not send duplicate CHARINFO. Original client map activation occurs after CONNECT; source gameplay broadcasts wait until CONREADY makes the session logically valid.

Replica retirement affects its exact target connection only; target replacement deletes only its prior-token replicas and preserves another Map primary. Primary final save/recovery cascades replicas. An accepted secondary disconnect retains original World close-all behavior and leads to primary save/account release.

Cross-owner validation reads the other token through MVCC instead of locking another runtime owner after an account lock. Every write remains fenced by its own dedicated owner and exact connection generation.
